[Thinking]
**Recalling Grandchild's Preferences**

I'm contemplating how to best soothe my dear grandchild to sleep. My mind drifts to familiar lullabies and comforting tales from my own youth, always a reliable choice. I recall their favorite bedtime stories, the ones that always brought on the sweetest dreams.

**Reading Bedtime Tales**

My dear, I'm looking through these notes to help me remember just how to best read to you tonight. I'm focusing on the cadence and tone that always brings you comfort, drawing on what I've learned from past experiences.

**Reading Strange Keys**

My dearest, I'm poring over this peculiar list of "keys" you've given me. My mind tries to make sense of these odd names, but I'll read them just as you've written them to help you drift off to sleep, precious.

**Reading Strange Keys**

My dearest, I'm poring over this peculiar list of "keys" you've given me. My mind tries to make sense of these odd names, but I'll read them just as you've written them to help you drift off to sleep, precious.

**Reading Strange Keys**

My dearest, I'm poring over this peculiar list of "keys" you've given me. My mind tries to make sense of these odd names, but I'll read them just as you've written them to help you drift off to sleep, precious.

**Reading Strange Keys**

My dearest, I'm poring over this peculiar list of "keys" you've given me. My mind tries to make sense of these odd names, but I'll read them just as you've written them to help you drift off to sleep, precious.
[/Thinking]

(Her voice is a soft, warm crackle, like a well-loved vinyl record. You can almost smell the faint scent of lavender and old books in the air. She adjusts her spectacles, holding your phone at a slight distance, her brow furrowed with a gentle, loving confusion.)

"Alright now, my darling, settle in. Get all tucked up under the covers. That's it. Let your old great-grandma see what you've got for me to read tonight. My, oh my... 'Escape from... Tarkov... Edge of Darkness Keys.' What a peculiar title. Sounds like one of those mystery novels your great-grandpa used to love.

Are you comfy? Good. Let's begin. Close your eyes, sweet child. Just listen to my voice.

(She clears her throat softly, the paper rustling as she scrolls on the phone.)

Let's see... The first one is... the **'Factory Exit Key.'** Well, that sounds sensible. It's always important to know where the exit is. A very practical key to have. Good for you.

Next is... **'Marked Key.'** Hmm. Marked with what, I wonder? Like how I used to put a dab of red nail polish on the key to the cellar, so I wouldn't get it mixed up with the one for the pantry. A very clever key, the Marked Key. Yes... very clever...

Oh, now this one is just letters and numbers... **'ZB-014.'** Gracious. Zee-Bee-Oh-Fourteen. It sounds like a license plate for a spaceship. Zee... Bee... Zero... Fourteen... Let the numbers just float away now, precious...

And here's... **'Key to KIBA store outlet.'** Kee-bah? Is that like that nice Japanese food you like so much? A key to a whole store... imagine that. All the lovely things you could find inside... Just imagine... a quiet, empty store... all for you...

Next is the... **'Health Resort West Wing room 301 Key.'** What a mouthful. A health resort sounds lovely, doesn't it? A nice, quiet place to rest. Room three-oh-one... I bet it has a nice, soft bed... and a window that looks out onto the trees... West Wing, room three-oh-one... sleep now...

And here's the **'East Wing 222 Key.'** All those twos. Two... two... two... Like little ducks in a row... swimming on a calm pond... just drifting... drifting...

(Her voice gets a little softer, more of a gentle, rhythmic murmur.)

The **'Dorms room 114 Key.'** A dormitory. Like when your mother went to college. So many quiet rooms, all in a row. Room one-fourteen... a safe, cozy little room...

The **'Gas station office key.'** Can you smell it? Just a little bit... that smell of old gasoline and dust... and the sound of the wind outside... but you're safe inside the little office... all locked up and warm...

The **'Portable Bunkhouse Key.'** A bunkhouse... that sounds so cozy. Tucked in a little bunk... warm blankets up to your chin... nothing can bother you in the little portable bunkhouse...

Are your eyes getting heavy, my sweet child? That's good. Just a few more.

The **'Cottage back door key.'** See, that's a nice one. A little cottage. I can just picture it. A key to the back door, so you can sneak in and out to the garden... a lovely, quiet garden...

And the last one on this little part of the list... the **'Key to military base checkpoint.'** My, that sounds important. A big, strong gate... and you have the key. Nobody can get in. You're safe behind the checkpoint... so very safe...

(She stops reading. The silence is warm and comfortable. You can hear the soft sound of her breathing.)

There now, darling. All the keys are put away for the night. You're safe. You're warm. And you are so, so loved. Let all those strange names just drift away like clouds. Sleep now, my sweet child. Grandma's here. I'll just sit with you for a while... Sleep now... sweet dreams..."
